title: uat-run/3
description: The run archive the capability ledger derives from. `uat-run/3` is `uat-run/2` plus four additions (SCHEMA.md §5.1): per-row `requirements`, per-row `observations[]`, the `infra` marker and `req` on a journal step entry. Everything `uat-run/2` carried is unchanged, so a v2 consumer keeps working; this schema describes the /3 shape and is what VALIDATOR.md L051 validates a supplied run against. A `uat-run/2` archive does NOT validate against it and is read in the synthesised compatibility mode instead.

meta.description: SCHEMA.md §7.1. Every field the configuration gate L023 compares is REQUIRED here: an absent field is a gate failure, and a run that cannot even state its own configuration is not evidence.

appCommit.description: The SUITE branch HEAD the run was taken on — compared to versionPin.suiteCommit, never to appSourceCommit.

observation.description: SCHEMA.md §5.1. One result for one requirement, or — for `unattributed` — one result for a failure that belongs to no requirement the row attributed.

requirementId.description: null ONLY on an `unattributed` observation: the failure happened outside every attributed assertion, so no requirement owns it.

attribution.description: `step` when an attributed assertion the journal records produced this result, `row` when the row itself did. A `fail` is ALWAYS `step` (review 6): see the clause below.

step.description: The step() name this observation reports on. On an `unattributed` observation it names the step the row FELL OVER IN when that step declares no requirement (L061) — the place is known even though no requirement owns the failure.

stepIndex.description: The step's 1-based position among the journal's `kind: "step"` entries. REQUIRED on a step-attributed observation: `(requirementId, stepIndex)` is the key an observation is identified by (SCHEMA.md §5.1, L057), so one without an index has no identity to be counted at.

assertion.description: The expect(…, "<message>") message of the assertion this observation reports on, when the step named one.

failedAssertion.description: The expect(…, "<message>") message of the assertion that FAILED. Matched by signature.assertion (§5.4).

allOf.description: An `unattributed` observation is row-attributed and names no requirement — it is exactly the failure no assertion owns. It may name a `step`, and only for the one shape L061 requires it in: the row fell over inside a journal step that declares no requirement, so the failure has a place but no owner. It never carries a `stepIndex`, because it reports on no attributed assertion and therefore indexes none.
Every other status names a requirement.
A step-attributed observation names its step AND its position: `(requirementId, stepIndex)` is the key L057 counts observations by, so both fields are required.

Review 6. A `fail` is a REQUIREMENT-OWNED failure, and the only thing that establishes ownership is an attributed assertion the journal recorded. So a `fail` observation is always `attribution: "step"` and always carries `step` + `stepIndex`: a requirement-owned failure is step-attributed, and a failure no assertion owns is `unattributed` (SCHEMA.md §5.1). The shape this forbids is a row-attributed `fail` for a requirement the row merely DECLARED — it manufactures a per-requirement failure out of a failure nobody owned, and, sitting beside the `unattributed` observation the real site owed, it outranks it in the §5.3 fold and can then be excused by a defect signature (§5.4).

The same rule stated from the attribution side, so the violation is reported against whichever field the author got wrong: `attribution: "row"` carries only `pass`, `skipped`, `not-run` (§5.1 rules 5 and 7) or `unattributed` (rule 6). Never `fail`.
A row-attributed observation that names a requirement has no step to name — the `unattributed` observation of the clause above is the one exception, and it never carries an index either way.
Only a failure carries a failedAssertion.

journalEntry.description: One entry of `UatTest.journal`. The `kind: "step"` entries, in order, ARE the sequence an observation's `stepIndex` indexes into (1-based); L061 ties every step-attributed observation to the entry at its index, and requires that entry's `req` to name the requirement the observation is credited with. Each `(step entry carrying req, id in that req)` pair owes exactly one observation at that index — the cardinality L057 counts (review 5, finding 2) — and it is the entry the failure site resolves to that decides how a failure is represented.

allOf.description: `req` is the step declaration of §5.1 and lives only on a step entry.

test.description: One Playwright row. `requirements`, `observations` and `req` on a journal step entry are the /3 additions. `requirements`, `observations` AND `journal` are all required: an absent declaration must be a schema failure rather than a silent empty set, and `journal` is what step attribution is checked AGAINST (L061, review 3 finding 4) — an attribution with no executed step behind it is an unverifiable claim, so a row that attributes to steps without recording them does not validate.

requirements.description: The row-level declaration, parsed from the `requirements` annotation. `[]` only on an infra row.

journal.description: Required. The executed journal — what step attribution is verified against (L061). `[]` is legal and means the row attributed nothing to a step.

failedDuring.description: WHERE the row failed — the failure SITE, and the evidence behind every `fail` attribution on the row (review 4, finding 2). A `step` site names the step and its 1-based position among the journal's step entries, and L061 RESOLVES it against the journal before it requires anything of the observations (review 5, finding 1): the entry at that index must carry that name, or the site is not reconcilable and the row is rejected. Once resolved, that entry's `req` decides the representation — a failing step that declares requirements owes a step-attributed `fail` for each of them and may carry no `unattributed` observation; a failing step that declares none owes exactly one `unattributed` observation naming that step, and no step-attributed `fail`. Every other kind happened outside every `step(page, name, fn, {req})`, so the row owes exactly one `unattributed` observation naming NO step (SCHEMA.md §5.1 rule 6). `between` is the reporter's current spelling for "after the last checkpoint" (`e2e/lib/summaryReporter.ts`) and is one of those non-step sites.

allOf.description: A step failure site names the step and its 1-based position, or L061 has nothing to compare a step-attributed fail against.
An infra row asserts no product behaviour, so it declares nothing and observes nothing.

A row that failed must say WHERE (review 4, finding 2). `status` is the raw Playwright fact the execution outcome is recomputed from (L060), so `failed`/`timedOut`/`interrupted` is exactly the set of rows whose recomputed outcome is `failed` or `expected-failure` — the rows where a failure actually occurred. `unexpected-pass` is not among them: its Playwright status is `passed`, so there is no failure site to record. Without `failedDuring` a failed row's attributions rest on nothing, and L061 rejects the row as `invalid` if no run schema was supplied to catch it here.
